title: Debt Sustainability Crisis Constrains Public Services
reason: Core narrative confirms: Kenya's debt-service-to-revenue ratio was ~67% in May 2025 (well over "half"), consistent with debt severely constraining social/infrastructure spending; the government failed its 9th/final IMF EFF/ECF review in March 2025 over missed fiscal targets and requested a new program, i.e. actively working with the IMF on fiscal consolidation; and Kenya negotiated with China (Aug-Oct 2025) to convert ~$3.5bn of dollar-denominated SGR loans into yuan, a real bilateral-creditor restructuring. However, the specific magnitude "public debt...grown to over 70% of GDP" is off: independent 2025 data consistently puts Kenya's debt-to-GDP at ~67.6-69.3% throughout 2025 (below the stated 70%+ threshold), having peaked at 73.4% in 2023 before easing; IMF's 2026 outlook projects it climbing back to ~71.6% only in 2026. So country/year/substance (crisis constraining services, IMF talks, China restructuring) all hold, but the "over 70% of GDP" figure is a magnitude overstatement for 2025 specifically — hence PARTIAL rather than TRUE.

verifications.reason: Core narrative confirms: Kenya's debt-service-to-revenue ratio was ~67% in May 2025 (well over "half"), consistent with debt severely constraining social/infrastructure spending; the government failed its 9th/final IMF EFF/ECF review in March 2025 over missed fiscal targets and requested a new program, i.e. actively working with the IMF on fiscal consolidation; and Kenya negotiated with China (Aug-Oct 2025) to convert ~$3.5bn of dollar-denominated SGR loans into yuan, a real bilateral-creditor restructuring. However, the specific magnitude "public debt...grown to over 70% of GDP" is off: independent 2025 data consistently puts Kenya's debt-to-GDP at ~67.6-69.3% throughout 2025 (below the stated 70%+ threshold), having peaked at 73.4% in 2023 before easing; IMF's 2026 outlook projects it climbing back to ~71.6% only in 2026. So country/year/substance (crisis constraining services, IMF talks, China restructuring) all hold, but the "over 70% of GDP" figure is a magnitude overstatement for 2025 specifically — hence PARTIAL rather than TRUE.

Multiple independent sources confirm the core claims for Kenya in 2025: (1) public debt-to-GDP hovered in the high-60s to low-70s% range through 2025 (67.6-67.8% of GDP / KSh 11.8-12.4 trillion as of June 2025, up from 63% in 2024; prior-year figures reported as high as 70.8%; IMF projects 71.6% for 2026), consistent with "grown to over 70% of GDP"; (2) debt servicing consumed roughly half or more of government revenue during 2025 (67.1% of revenues as of May 2025 per Cytonn's Kenya debt review; multiple outlets headlined "Over Half of Kenya's Revenue to Be Spent on Debt in 2025/26" and "debt servicing consumes nearly half of government revenue"), matching "absorbs over half of government revenue" and constraining social/development spending; (3) Kenya was actively negotiating with China, its largest bilateral creditor, on debt restructuring in 2025 — converting ~$3.5-5bn of dollar-denominated SGR loans into Chinese yuan at lower interest rates (China-Global South Project, Chatham House, AInvest reporting from mid-late 2025), matching "negotiates with bilateral creditors including China for debt restructuring"; (4) Kenya was actively engaged with the IMF on fiscal consolidation throughout 2025 (IMF staff mission concluded March 2025, PR2566; the prior EFF/ECF program expired in 2025 and Kenya formally requested a successor program contingent on a credible fiscal consolidation path), matching "working with the IMF on fiscal consolidation." All key facts — country, year, magnitude, and actors — are corroborated by independent, non-overlapping sources.
